evidence.snippet: I'm seeing the sensor list now—looks like 4 temperature, 2 vibration, 1 power sensor. That's manageable for BOM. But I want to confirm: are we doing custom PCB or using off-the-shelf modules?

From manufacturing perspective, I need clarity on sensor count and types early—that drives BOM and assembly complexity. Also, we should lock the enclosure form factor and IP rating now so design can move forward without rework.
We should outsource the PCB. I've already reached out to two vendors who can turn around a prototype in 5 days. Cost is reasonable and it frees up our team to focus on assembly and testing.
I've reviewed the BOM. We can save about 12% by switching to a lower-cost compute module and using a smaller storage capacity. That brings us closer to the target.

evidence.snippet: Let me run the math: at 5-second intervals with 7 sensors, we're about 100KB per minute. 512MB gives us ~85 hours, which is actually okay. I'll propose 1GB as a compromise—gives us 170 hours of buffer.
Yes, I'll build in sensor health checks and graceful degradation. If a sensor fails, we log an error and continue collecting from others. That's part of the edge software design.
Great. I'll set up a dev environment with a simulator for the sensors so I can start coding the edge software in parallel. That way, I'm not blocked waiting for hardware.

From the data side, I'll need to understand what sensors we're collecting from and how frequently. I'm working on the architecture spec (A4) but want to make sure we align on latency and buffering requirements.

evidence.snippet: I've been thinking about the mechanical constraints. The enclosure needs to fit in tight spaces on production lines, so compact form factor is critical. I'll sketch a few concepts this week and share CAD outlines for feedback.

Here are the three enclosure concepts I promised. Option A is aluminum with passive cooling—compact, robust, but heavier. Option B is plastic with aluminum heat sink insert—lighter, cheaper, but thermal margin is tighter. Option C is hybrid: plastic body with aluminum top plate for sensor mounting.

Compact IP65 is tight but doable. I'll have three enclosure concepts sketched by tomorrow morning. Aluminum will be my baseline for thermal, but I'll also show plastic option for cost comparison. Electrical, can you confirm the heat dissipation budget so I can size the enclosure properly?

evidence.snippet: On electrical side, I'll need to see the sensor specs and power budget before I finalize the schematics. Also, we need to confirm which safety standards apply—IEC 61010 or IEC 61508 depending on the control function.

I've finalized the schematics and run them against the safety checklist (A2). No critical gaps—all grounding, surge protection, and isolation requirements are met. I prefer Option C: hybrid design gives us good thermal performance without the weight penalty.
Heat dissipation should be minimal—maybe 2-3W max from the PCB. I'll have the preliminary schematic by tomorrow EOD. That will give you the component footprint and power distribution layout.
